Part 1 · The stack
One origin: the browser only talks to Vite
Browser
React SPA, access token in memory
Vite :5173
serves the app, proxies /api
Django :8000
DRF + SimpleJWT, /api/v1/
Postgres :5433
PostgreSQL 17 in Docker
Why one origin? The refresh cookie stays first-party and CSRF works without CORS. In production a reverse proxy serves frontend/dist and forwards /api to Django on one domain.
Source: frontend/vite.config.ts · docker-compose.yml · CLAUDE.md (“served from one origin”)

Part 1 · Frontend
Ant Design + Tailwind: one job each
Ant Design 6
Owns components and colours: forms, tables, modals, tags.
token: { colorPrimary: BRAND_COLOR,
  borderRadius: 8, fontFamily }
ConfigProvider in PreferencesProvider.tsx
Tailwind 4
Only layout and spacing: flex, grid, gap, padding.
@import 'tailwindcss/theme.css' layer(theme);
@import 'tailwindcss/utilities.css' layer(utilities);
index.css: preflight skipped on purpose
Why: Tailwind’s reset (preflight) would fight Ant Design’s base styles. Splitting the jobs avoids two styling systems clashing.

Part 1 · Frontend
Axios: one client, safe tokens
// api/client.ts (shortened): the only Axios instance
export const api = axios.create({
  baseURL: '/api/v1', withCredentials: true,
  xsrfCookieName: 'csrftoken',
  xsrfHeaderName: 'X-CSRFToken',
})
let accessToken: string | null = null // memory only
refreshInFlight ??= api.post('/auth/refresh/', …)
Access token (5 min) in JS memory. Never in localStorage.
On 401 the interceptor refreshes once and retries the request.
Shared refresh: parallel calls wait for one refresh. Two would log the user out, because the server rotates tokens.
Source: frontend/src/api/client.ts · CLAUDE.md, Auth model · Lesson 07
Part 1 · Frontend
React Router: guards, safe redirects, URL state
Route guards
ProtectedRoute sends guests to /login and remembers where they were going. GuestRoute keeps signed-in users out of /login.
Safe redirect
from.startsWith('/') &&
!from.startsWith('//')
Blocks open redirects such as //evil.example.
Filters in the URL
/?status=done&search=milk&page=2 survives a reload and can be shared. Bad values are dropped.
Source: features/auth/RouteGuards.tsx · features/auth/redirect.ts · features/tasks/query.ts · Lessons 09–10

Part 1 · Backend
DRF + SimpleJWT + PostgreSQL
Django REST Framework
Task.objects.filter(owner=user)
Every query is scoped to the user. Another user’s task gives 404, not 403, so IDs don’t leak.
SimpleJWT
Access token: 5 min, in memory. Refresh token: 7 days, httpOnly cookie on /api/v1/auth/, rotated and blacklisted on every use. CSRF on refresh and logout.
PostgreSQL 17
Docker on :5433. CHECK constraints and owner-first indexes. The ERD and a scaling roadmap are in docs/erd.md.
Never disable CSRF, permissions, throttling or the ownership filter “to make something work”.
Source: backend/tasks/views.py:29–30 · backend/config/settings.py (SIMPLE_JWT) · docs/erd.md · Lessons 02–05

Motion: animation that explains a change
# 1. pin a version older than 2 weeks
npm view motion time --json | tail -8
npm install --save-exact motion@14.0.0
# 2. wrap the app once (PreferencesProvider)
<MotionConfig reducedMotion="user">
  <LazyMotion features={loadMotionFeatures} strict>
# 3. use the light components everywhere
import * as m from 'motion/react-m'
<m.div initial={{ opacity: 0, y: 12 }}
  animate={{ opacity: 1, y: 0 }} />
Animate: things appearing, leaving, a count changing, a task done.
Never: table rows, loops, bounce on data.

Guarded

Part 2 · Helper 3 · 21st.dev
21st.dev: take the idea, not the code
21st.dev is a gallery of React components built on shadcn + Radix + Tailwind colours.
Our rule: Ant Design owns components and colours. Pasting its code would add a second styling system.
So: browse for ideas → rebuild with Ant Design tokens. Here: glow + dot grid + split sign-in.

Part 3 · The Claude setup
CLAUDE.md: the rules Claude reads every session
Cross-package rules
  • Plan first: a spec before multi-file work
  • types.ts mirrors serializers
  • erd.md mirrors the models
  • New logic needs a test
Auth model
  • Access token in memory
  • Refresh in httpOnly cookie, rotated
  • CSRF on refresh and logout
  • “Do not change without discussion”
Never
  • Commit .env or secrets
  • Tokens in localStorage
  • Disable CSRF or permissions
  • Edit an applied migration
  • Reset the DB unasked
Tip: keep it short and specific. Each package has its own CLAUDE.md with its stack, commands and conventions.
Source: CLAUDE.md · backend/CLAUDE.md · frontend/CLAUDE.md

Part 3 · Our project commands
/dev → /check → /review → /commit
/dev
haiku
Creates .env if missing, starts DB, API and Vite, waits for both URLs
/check
haiku
Runs scripts/check.sh, reports PASS / FAIL / NOT RUN. Edits nothing
/review
default model
Diff vs the 3 CLAUDE.md files, violations with file:line. Edits nothing
/commit
sonnet
Message for the staged diff, checks for secrets. Never commits unasked
.claude/commands/check.md
model: haiku
description: Run every backend and frontend check …
Run all project checks … Do not modify any files.
⚠ Name clash: Claude Code also has a built-in /review (alias of /code-review). Check which one runs with /help.
Source: .claude/commands/dev.md, check.md, review.md, commit.md · Lesson 13

Part 3 · Agents and hooks
Agents check the work. Hooks guard it.
Agents · .claude/agents/
backend-reviewer: read-only; security, ownership, migrations, tests
frontend-reviewer: read-only; tokens, i18n parity, API client, styling
test-writer: adds pytest, Vitest or Playwright tests, never changes the code under test
Hooks · settings.json
Before Edit/Write: block-secrets.sh refuses writes to .env files
After Edit/Write: format-on-edit.sh runs ruff on backend Python
permissions.allow: tests, lint and scripts run without a prompt
Source: .claude/agents/*.md · .claude/settings.json · .claude/hooks/*.sh
Part 3 · Prompt helpers
Rough idea → good prompt → new session
1
/prompt-master
Turns “let’s build a slide lesson” into a full prompt with context, rules and stop points
2
/copy
Puts the generated prompt on your clipboard
3
/clear + paste
Fresh context, then paste. The prompt says “plan first, stop for approval”
Why it works: the agent gets everything in turn one, including when to stop and ask.
Source: this lesson was planned this way · Lesson 15 (writing prompts) · /prompt-master is a personal skill in ~/.claude/skills
